Anya: FYI — Marketplace onboarding for eu-west is delayed by the partner. They just pushed the provisioning window out by ~10 business days, which collides with our EU Dedicated commit. We need to decide buffer/SLA fallback. /cc @Kevin @Marie
Kevin: Ugh. Any reason? customs/manifest or partner capacity?
PartnersBot: Reservation update: partner-resv-847 changed ETA from 2026-04-12 to 2026-04-26. (auto-notify)
Leo: Partner ops said it's a customs hold at the EU crossdock, manifests ok but clearance backlog. That impacts 3 racks (48 GPUs) scheduled for first EU wave. We should plan a geo-stagger and move 2 racks to US standby until cleared.
Marie: If we move capacity to US, we need to confirm latency SLO impact for EU tenants and update canary rules. Also need to push the joint announcement window. Suggested fallback schedule:
```
canary (US) rollout: 2026-04-15
EU staggered cutover: 2026-04-29 (+buffer)
public announcement: 2026-05-06 -> consider +1 week
``` 
Kevin: Numbers check: moving 2 racks = +15% cost for cross-region egress and burst. If we apply a 14-day SLA buffer we cover most customs delays. Can SI partner confirm they can accept a delayed on-prem install? Asking @Leo to ping SI PM.
Anya: Linking manifests and carrier ETA here: https://files.redwood.test/partner-manifests/847 and the partner's updated ETA table. My proposal: 1) activate US standby (immediate), 2) hold EU announcement until we get customs clear + one buffer week, 3) offer customers optional EU beta with best-effort latency. If SI cannot accept delay we escalate to partner ops.
Leo: Pinged SI PM — they can accept a 7-10 day install slip but prefer we avoid changing contractual delivery dates. I'll push request for priority customs clearance. :pray:
Marie: OK - I'll inform comms/legal and draft a revised announcement timeline. Action items: confirm SI acceptance (Leo), finalize cost uplift delta (Kevin), and update contract addendum if needed (Anya). (thumbsup)
